CATHOTEL"
Dearest Debs;
I am really getting very fond of this
little old typewriter, it is easier for me to write
on it than by hand because as you know my arm is
still not so good - that is it hurts me a little to
write at much length. So I hope you dont mind this.
I have just this minute received your
6th and 7th letters together with one from Bo. What
delayed them since yesterday I do not know. Want to
take this opportunity to answer some questions in
yours of the 14th. The ST.L.G.&Q are running true to
form I fear. Hope you will have ben able to get that
account straightened out by this time. Also hope that
Mary Love will be able to get McCurdy to pay the bill
for water bur agree with you that we ahould not coll-
ect under the lease if it will jeopardise the lease.
The important thing now is to keep the house rented.
I have not heard yet about the sale of the two acres
actually being completed and payment received. Hope
Ralph was able to handle that for us.
Poor Henry he has a real problem with
Kitty. As you say she is just plain poison, and is
getting worse all the time.
The Income tax matter is
OK. I should have told you about that but it was one
of the things I failed to do. The Treasury Dept. was
trying to take advantage of a technicality to cheat
me out of $ 2,000.00 and I think that by filing an
ammended return I will ultimately be able to get some
money back which I have already paid. Your Father's
auditor fixed up the ammended return for me and it is
just possible that he may be able to represent my int-
ersts without waiting until 1934. You might send this
letter, or this part of it to your Father with a re-
port of what Aud's lawyer wrote for you to the author-
ities in Washington. Re
Regarding Ralph's assignment to our children
I wish you would write to the ST.L Union and tell them
that you know I do not want that done.
Lots + lots of horr. Bir
